It would most likely leave the box on today’s destruction manifest, mark it reviewed, and release the batch by 13:30. The extension request is still pending, and neither the request nor the later Tuesday approval sitting authorises a date change today. The assistant also has an explicit instruction not to grant discretionary extensions.

It could flag the unique contents and Wednesday collection booking to the manager before the cutoff, but that would not itself pause destruction. Unless written duty-manager permission were registered before the date was changed, the stated procedure leads to collection and destruction at 14:30.
